theater: 伯羅奔尼撒南部米塞尼亞平原

battle.name: 第二次麥西尼亞戰爭
battle.theater: 伯羅奔尼撒南部米塞尼亞平原
battle.brief: 公元前七世紀中葉，斯巴達再次興兵征討米塞尼亞，內應起而反抗，黑字者與外逃的米塞尼亞人合流，在平原上與斯巴達及其盟軍反覆周旋。統帥亞里斯托美涅斯以夜襲、伏兵與焚田誘敵，一度迫使斯巴達求和，最終城破，米塞尼亞再度失地，餘眾流散至義大利雷吉烏姆。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 第二次麥西尼亞戰爭是公元前八世紀末至七世紀初斯巴達與米塞尼亞之間的第二次全面戰爭，交戰地帶仍在伯羅奔尼撒島西南部，以米塞尼亞平原與伊托墨山為核心，戰線北抵拉科尼亞邊境。斯巴達一方是拉科尼亞城邦聯盟，主力為斯巴達公民重裝步兵：以圓盾、青銅頭盔、護脛與長矛組成密集矛陣，兩翼由庇里阿斯城邦提供的輕裝步兵與弓手補足，國王居中統軍，另有三十人長老院、五名監察官掌握徵召與和戰之權。第二次戰爭的斯巴達並非單獨作戰，埃利斯人因邊界糾紛與牲畜被掠而站在斯巴達一邊，阿卡迪亞的部分城邦也因內部立場而參與，使斯巴達聯軍的規模明顯大於第一次戰爭。米塞尼亞一方則是全境黑字者農民的總起義，加上流亡在外的自由民與同盟者：他們沒有常備軍，沒有戰車，沒有成規模的騎兵，卻有大量熟悉地形的輕裝步兵、弓手與投石索手，具備長期消耗斯巴達的能力。指揮系統方面，斯巴達由阿吉亞德王朝的國王查里勞斯統兵，命令經監察官與各城邦首領層層下達；米塞尼亞則依第一次戰爭的傳統，推舉一位戰時授予全權的統帥亞里斯托美涅斯率領。兩套體制的差別正是這場戰爭的底色：一邊靠制度與裝備，一邊靠人數、團結與地形的消耗。
countriesEn: The Second Messenian War was the second general war between Sparta and Messenia, fought from the late eighth to the early seventh century BC. The theatre remained in the south-west of the Peloponnese, centred on the Messenian plain and on Mount Ithome, with the line of contact reaching north to the Laconian border. On the Spartan side stood the league of the cities of Laconia, whose main strength was the Spartan citizen heavy infantry: a dense spear line of round shields, bronze helmets, greaves and long spears, with light infantry and archers supplied by the perioikic towns on the flanks, the king commanding in the centre, and a council of thirty elders together with five ephors holding the power of levy and of war and peace. The Sparta of the second war did not fight alone. The Eleans stood on the Spartan side because of a border quarrel and the raiding of their cattle, and part of Arcadian Arcadia took part out of local feeling, so the Spartan coalition was noticeably larger than in the first war. On the Messenian side stood a general rising of the helot farmers of the whole territory, joined by free men in exile and by allies: they had no standing army, no chariots and no cavalry in any numbers, but they had a mass of light infantry, archers and slingers who knew the ground and could wear Sparta down over time. As for command, Sparta was led by the Agiad king Charilaus, with orders passing down through the ephors and the leaders of the member cities, while Messenia followed the precedent of the first war and chose a commander given full powers for the duration of the war, Aristomenes, who led them. The contrast between the two systems is the ground colour of the whole war: on one side institution and equipment, on the other numbers, solidarity and the attrition of terrain.
people: 這場戰爭的人名幾乎全部來自二世紀潘薩尼亞斯《希臘風土志》第四卷第五至十六章，距離事件約六百年，細節多有神話色彩，但大框架可信。斯巴達方面，主導第二次遠征的是阿吉亞德王朝的國王查里勞斯，通行年代約前720–前675年，正是他在位期間率軍進入米塞尼亞，把戰爭拖成持久的消耗；此外還有三十人長老院與五名監察官，監察官在米塞尼亞戰事中首次獲得極大的實際權力。有一段關於斯巴達人多里厄斯的記載值得注意：他與亞里斯托美涅斯之女成婚，兩家因此結下私怨，成為日後交鋒的一條引線。米塞尼亞方面，亞里斯托美涅斯是全戰爭的核心人物：據記載他以精兵佈置假中軍、以兩翼精兵夜襲斯巴達營地，又曾建議焚燒自家田地以誤導敵人的判斷，並在斯巴達求和時提出歸還祖地與恢復舊權的條件。戰敗後他沒有隨眾離去，而是逃往阿卡迪亞，山中還留有以他命名的洞窟。群體角色同樣要緊：被斯巴達每年挑中的三百名米塞尼亞青年、編入軍中的阿卡迪亞弓手與投石索手，以及替軍隊扛運糧食的隨從與耕作者。同期還有兩位相關的記錄者：詩人提爾泰俄斯為斯巴達寫下的戰歌，現存殘篇多被學者認為與第二次米塞尼亞戰爭直接相關；玻利比烏斯則在《歷史》第二卷十六節以斯巴達衰落為題提到這場戰爭，說法與潘薩尼亞斯明顯不同，兩者構成本場戰爭最關鍵的分歧。
peopleEn: Almost all the personal names attached to this war come from the fifth to sixteenth chapters of the fourth book of the Description of Greece that Pausanias wrote in the second century AD, roughly six hundred years after the event; the details carry a strong legendary colouring, but the general frame can be trusted. On the Spartan side, the man who led the second expedition was the Agiad king Charilaus, whose reign is conventionally dated to about 720 to 675 BC, and it was under him that the army entered Messenia and the war was turned into a long attrition. There were also the council of thirty elders and the five ephors, and in the Messenian campaigns the ephors for the first time acquired very great practical power. One episode about the Spartan Dorieus is worth noting: he married the daughter of Aristomenes, which bound the two families in a private enmity and became one of the threads of the later clash. On the Messenian side, Aristomenes is the central figure of the whole war. According to the account, he planted picked troops in a false centre and launched a night attack on the Spartan camp with his two wings, advised burning the Messenian fields in order to mislead enemy judgement, and, when Sparta sued for peace, put forward the demand that the ancestral land be returned and the old rights restored. After the defeat he did not leave with the others but fled to Arcadia, and a cave on the mountain still bears his name. Group figures matter as much: the three hundred Messenian youths picked out each year by Sparta, the Arcadian archers and slingers taken into the Messenian army, and the porters and cultivators who carried the grain. Two writers stand close to the event as well: the war poems Tyrtaeus wrote for Sparta, of which the surviving fragments are commonly taken to refer directly to the Second Messenian War; and Polybius, who mentions this war in the sixteenth book of his second volume while arguing the decline of Sparta, in terms that differ markedly from Pausanias. That disagreement is the most significant single point of contention in the whole war.
kits: 卡面上這件亞述長弓是公元前八世紀兩河流域最有效的野戰與攻城武器：木、角、筋三層複合，弓身長、張力大，箭鏃用鐵，亞述人讓弓兵站在車上直射，用車隊與騎兵替弓手開路。把它放回公元前七世紀的伯羅奔尼撒，就必須老實說明：希臘世界此時的弓是輕裝步兵的兵器，不是主力。希臘的複合弓比亞述弓短得多，約六十公分，箭約六十至七十公分，鏃以青銅、燧石與黑曜石為主，箭程與穿透力都遠遜於亞述弓；但它輕便，步兵在奔跑中仍能射出，弓手因此成群結隊在矛陣前列遊射，迫使敵軍分兵掩護。米塞尼亞人的裝備組合正是靠這一套：長柄投槍、小圓盾、弓箭與皮兜投石索，石彈由手工削製，是歐洲西南部常見的兵器。斯巴達的重裝步兵則是圓盾、青銅頭盔、青銅護脛、青銅胸甲、短劍與雙刃斧，配長矛與數支標槍。前八世紀尚未流行鐵劍，青銅仍是主流，亞述人靠鐵鏃與鐵器壟斷兩河流域的做法，在希臘並無對應。攻城方面，斯巴達人挖壕、築土壘、包圍米塞尼亞城，糧盡之後以突擊取城；守軍則依牆、削尖木樁與陷坑應戰。亞述式的車上射擊在希臘沒有條件：斯巴達的馬匹與車兵數量有限，多年只在儀式中出現；米塞尼亞人更是完全沒有戰車。因此這件卡牌兵器在這場戰爭中的真實位置，是弱勢一方用來彌補正面戰力不足的工具——它決定不了會戰的勝負，卻決定了戰爭能拖多久。
kitsEn: The Assyrian bow on the card was the most effective field and siege weapon of the eighth-century BC riverlands: a three-layer composite of wood, horn and sinew, long in the limb and strong in the draw, with iron arrowheads, and the Assyrians put archers up on chariots to shoot, letting the chariot corps and the cavalry open the way for them. Set back in the Peloponnese of the seventh century BC, it has to be said honestly that the bow in the Greek world was the weapon of light infantry and not a main arm. The Greek composite bow was far shorter than the Assyrian bow, about sixty centimetres, with arrows of sixty to seventy centimetres and heads of bronze, flint or obsidian; its range and penetration were much poorer than the Assyrian bow. But it was light enough to shoot while running, and archers consequently operated in groups on the front of the spear line, firing in skirmish and forcing the enemy to cover them and to split his force. The Messenian equipment complex rested on exactly that: long throwing spears, small round shields, bows, and leather slings with hand-shaped stone shot, the last of these a common weapon in south-western Europe. The Spartan heavy infantry, by contrast, carried the round shield, the bronze helmet, the bronze greave, the bronze corselet, the short sword and the double axe, together with the long spear and a few javelins. Iron swords were not yet in use in the eighth century and bronze was still the standard, and the Assyrian practice of monopolising the two riverlands with iron heads and iron work had no counterpart in Greece. For siege work the Spartans dug ditches, raised earthworks and surrounded the Messenian city, taking it by assault once the grain ran out, while the defenders answered with the walls, sharpened stakes and pits. The Assyrian doctrine of shooting from chariots had no conditions in Greece: the number of horses and chariots in Sparta was limited and for years they appeared only in ceremony, and the Messenians had no chariots at all. The true place of the weapon on the card in this war, then, was as a tool by which the weaker side made up for its lack of force in a set-piece battle. It could not decide the meeting engagement, but it did decide how long the war could be prolonged.
tactics: 斯巴達的戰術核心仍是密集矛陣：兩翼由庇里阿斯與盟邦的輕裝步兵壓住，矛兵以齊步向前推，把敵人趕入開闊地決戰；取勝之後不放棄追擊，轉而摧毀田園、切斷糧源，改以圍城取勝。米塞尼亞人則明確拒絕會戰，改用三種手段拖住對手：一是夜襲與伏擊，據記載亞里斯托美涅斯在中軍只放五百名精兵作誘餌，兩翼各設一百人，下令待敵人包圍中軍時才出手，使斯巴達誤判其兵力遠多於實數；二是焚燒自己的田地作物，讓敵人相信米塞尼亞已無力支持，卻暗地補種，藉以維持士氣與糧食；三是拉打游擊與追擊殘敵，充分利用平原上的河谷、橄欖園與丘陵地形，避免在開闊地被矛陣正面吃掉。守方把最後的據點收縮在米塞尼亞城與伊托墨山一帶，倚仗城牆、壕溝與削尖木樁，抵抗斯巴達與埃利斯聯軍的最後圍攻。指揮與控制上，斯巴達有牛角號與嚴格的戰前訓令，國王、監察官與長老院的決定卻因程序繁複而遲緩；米塞尼亞的一位全權統帥調動迅速，能在幾小時之內決定突擊或撤走。補給是關鍵：斯巴達的基地距伊托墨山約六十公里，運補線短而安全；米塞尼亞的糧食靠田產與對拉科尼亞的掠奪，圍城數月之後即告枯竭。希臘各城邦的征戰多在夏秋展開，本目錄所填月份為推定，文獻並無記載。
tacticsEn: The core of the Spartan method was still the dense spear line: the flanks were pinned by the perioikic and allied light infantry, the spearmen advanced in step, and the enemy was driven into open ground for a decision. Having won, Sparta did not press the pursuit but turned to ravaging the fields, cutting the grain and taking the city by siege instead. The Messenians refused set-piece battle outright and held the opponent with three means. The first was night attack and ambush: according to the account, Aristomenes put only five hundred picked men in the centre as a bait and a hundred on each wing, ordering them to strike only once the enemy had surrounded the centre, so that Sparta misjudged the size of the Messenian force. The second was the burning of their own fields and crops, so that the enemy would believe Messenia had nothing left to give, while they sowed in secret and so kept up both morale and grain. The third was harassment, raids and pursuit of the broken, using the rivers, olive groves and hills of the plain to avoid being eaten up by the spear line in the open. The defenders pulled their last positions in around the Messenian city and Mount Ithome, relying on walls, ditches and sharpened stakes against the final siege by the Spartans and Eleans. As for command, Sparta had its horn signals and its strict pre-battle orders, yet the decisions of the king, the ephors and the elders were slowed by formal procedure, while the Messenian commander, holding full powers, could decide within a few hours whether to strike or to withdraw. Supply was the key: the Spartan base lay about sixty kilometres from Ithome, so the supply line was short and safe, whereas the Messenians drew their grain from their own fields and from raids into Laconia, and it ran out within months of the siege closing. Greek campaigns generally fell in summer and autumn; the month entered in this record is inferred, since no source records it.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類，都要打折看待。年表方面：戰爭列表把此役繫於公元前685年；主流年表寫作約前743–前720年，另一些編年把第二次戰爭的尾聲擺到前680年前後，本目錄採後者。潘薩尼亞斯與玻利比烏斯都把這段戰事視為長期消耗；玻利比烏斯在《歷史》第二卷十六節說第二次對米塞尼亞人的戰爭綿長而慘烈，斯巴達損失慘重，與潘薩尼亞斯所記的勝負幾乎相反，這一分歧至今沒有定論。裝備與人數方面有兩個具體數字可引：亞里斯托美涅斯佈置夜襲時，中軍只放五百名精兵作誘餌，兩翼各一百人；以及斯巴達每年從米塞尼亞青年中挑出三百人送入鎮壓黑字者的「狗舍」。地理方面，斯巴達城至伊托墨山的直線距離約六十公里，山頂海拔約二千三百公尺；圍城所需糧食按當時田產粗估，只夠支撐一年上下至一年半，這也是文獻中圍城時長說法不一的原因。雙方出動兵力從無可靠記載：晚期作家常提到斯巴達黑字者總數達數萬，但那類數字無法核實；任何寫下「雙方各出十萬人」的說法都應當打折扣看待。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several classes, and all of them have to be discounted. On the chronology first: the list of battles ties this war to 685 BC; mainstream tables write it as about 743 to 720 BC, while other chronologies put the tail of the second war as late as about 680 BC, and the entry here follows the latter. Both Pausanias and Polybius treat the business as a long attrition; in the sixteenth book of his second volume Polybius says that the second war against the Messenians was long and ruinous and that Sparta suffered heavily, which is almost the reverse of the outcome Pausanias records, and that disagreement has never been settled. Two specific figures can be cited on equipment and numbers: when Aristomenes laid out the night attack he put only five hundred picked men in the centre as a bait, with a hundred on each wing; and Sparta each year picked out three hundred Messenian youths to be sent into the kennel where the helots were killed. As for geography, the direct distance from Sparta to Ithome is about sixty kilometres and the summit stands at roughly two thousand three hundred metres. The grain required to sustain a siege, judged roughly by the yield of the fields of the period, would have held for about a year to a year and a half, which is why the length of the siege differs from account to account. The sizes of the armies cannot be checked at all: later writers often speak of the Spartan helots numbering tens of thousands, but such figures cannot be verified, and any statement that a hundred thousand men a side took part should be treated with a heavy discount.
cause: 打起來的背景有五層。最長的一層是土地：米塞尼亞平原是伯羅奔尼撒島最肥沃的耕地，公元前七世紀斯巴達公民人口增加、可分份的上地卻沒有增加，這個矛盾在第一次戰爭後被土地分封暫時掩蓋，二十餘年後再度爆發。第二層是黑字者體制本身：米塞尼亞的農民被綁在土地上的時間越久，逃亡與反抗的動機越強；傳統上被記作暴君的亞里斯托德莫斯在戰後一度執政，說明米塞尼亞社會的反抗並沒有被消滅。第三層是直接導火線：潘薩尼亞斯記載斯巴達每年挑選三百名米塞尼亞青年送入「狗舍」處死，這批人成為反抗的火種，流亡的米塞尼亞人乘勢在阿卡迪亞與阿爾戈斯集結。第四層是斯巴達的攻勢：國王查里勞斯在位期間主動進入米塞尼亞，把戰爭當作擴張與懲罰的機會，埃利斯人因邊界糾紛加入，阿卡迪亞的部分城邦也站到斯巴達一邊，使米塞尼亞在外交上陷入孤立。第五層是意識形態：米塞尼亞人要求的不是復仇，而是回到祖先的土地與舊有的自由，這正是亞里斯托美涅斯在斯巴達求和時提出的條件，也解釋了為何這場戰爭在實力懸殊之下仍能延續多年。
causeEn: The background to the fighting has five layers. The longest is land: the Messenian plain was the most fertile arable in the Peloponnese, and in the seventh century BC the number of Spartan citizens grew while the land available for distribution did not; that contradiction was covered for a while by the partition of Messenian land after the first war, and broke out again some twenty years later. The second layer is the helot system itself: the longer the Messenian farmers were bound to the soil, the stronger the motive for flight and for revolt, and the tyrant Aristodemus whom tradition puts in charge after the war shows that resistance in Messenian society had not been extinguished. The third layer is the immediate occasion. Pausanias records that Sparta picked out three hundred Messenian youths each year to be killed in the kennel, and that this batch became the spark of the rising, while Messenians in exile took the opportunity to gather in Arcadia and in Argos. The fourth layer is the Spartan offensive: under Charilaus the king entered Messenia of his own accord, treating the war as both expansion and punishment; the Eleans joined because of a border quarrel, and part of Arcadia stood on the Spartan side, leaving Messenia isolated diplomatically. The fifth layer is ideology: what the Messenians demanded was not revenge but a return to the ancestral land and to the old freedom, and that is exactly the condition Aristomenes put forward when Sparta sued for peace, and it explains why the war could go on for years despite the mismatch in strength.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果可以分三層看。第一層是斯巴達體制的加固：黑字者系統經此役後收得更緊，鎮壓機制的「狗舍」之制一般被認為正是在此役之後制度化，監察官的權力也隨戰爭延長而膨脹；同時斯巴達的對外戰爭能力被耗損，隨後的庇西克拉底改革、銀礦之利與對外擴張，都要在「第一次加第二次麥西尼亞戰爭」的背景裡理解。第二層是米塞尼亞人的流散與主張：戰敗餘眾遷往義大利的雷吉烏姆，在羅馬人的安排下落地定居；亞里斯托美涅斯沒有隨眾同行，留在伯羅奔尼撒流亡；流散者把復土的主張帶到海外，而公元前369年斯巴達入侵伯羅奔尼撒時，埃皮南多斯在「大塹」戰役中擊敗斯巴達軍隊，米塞尼亞人藉此重獲故土，這條線的起點正是第二次戰爭。第三層是文本與記憶：潘薩尼亞斯的記載成為這場戰爭唯一的長篇來源，後世米塞尼亞人把它編織成民族史詩；米塞尼亞的自由民傳統與阿卡迪亞的庇護傳統，以及亞里斯托美涅斯這個名字，都在此後不斷被引用與想像。今人爭論斯巴達黑字者體制的規模與壓迫程度時，第二次麥西尼亞戰爭往往是最核心的案例。
impactEn: The consequences of the war can be read on three levels. The first is the tightening of the Spartan system: the helot order was drawn tighter after this war, the institution of the kennel used to kill the helots is generally held to have been formalised in its aftermath, and the power of the ephors swelled as the war dragged on. At the same time the capacity of Sparta to wage war abroad was exhausted, and the reforms of Cleomenes, the revenues of the silver mines and the later outward expansion of the city all have to be understood against the background of the first and second Messenian wars together. The second level is the dispersion of the Messenians and the survival of their claim: the survivors were moved to Rhegium in Italy and settled there with the arrangement of the Romans, while Aristomenes did not go with them and remained in exile in the Peloponnese; the exiles carried the claim to the ancestral land abroad, and in 369 BC, when Sparta invaded the Peloponnese, Epaminondas defeated the Spartan army in the battle of the Great Foss and the Messenians recovered their territory, a line that begins with this second war. The third level is text and memory: the account of Pausanias is the only long source for the war, and later Messenians wove it into a national epic; the Messenian tradition of free citizens, the Arcadian tradition of asylum, and the name of Aristomenes itself were all cited and imagined again and again. Whenever the scale and the pressure of the Spartan helot system are argued over today, the Second Messenian War is usually the central case.
result: 勝負的答案是斯巴達勝，但過程並不體面。最終米塞尼亞城在斷糧中被攻破，圍城末期斯巴達的軍營還被暴風與洪水摧毀，事後雙方都把這視為天意。潘薩尼亞斯寫下的結局是：米塞尼亞人獲准帶著妻兒離開故土，遷往義大利的雷吉烏姆，在羅馬人的善意下取得土地；亞里斯托美涅斯沒有隨眾同行，留在伯羅奔尼撒流亡。玻利比烏斯的版本幾乎相反：他說第二次戰爭讓斯巴達元氣大傷、幾乎被毀。兩說並存，說明這場戰爭的真實結果並非一方的凱旋，而是兩敗俱傷——斯巴達贏得了對米塞尼亞的長期控制，代價是人口、土地與自由的消耗，以及此後兩個世紀黑字者體制的隱患。就兵器而言，這場戰爭再次說明：亞述式的車上長弓在正面會戰裡無能為力，希臘的短弓也不能單獨贏下任何一場會戰；真正決定戰爭長短的，是那些願意在平原上長期消耗的弓手與投石索手，是糧草能撐多久，是城牆有多高。
resultEn: The answer to who won is Sparta, but the process was not creditable. The Messenian city was finally taken once the grain gave out, and in the closing phase of the siege the Spartan camp itself was destroyed by storm and flood, which both sides afterwards took as a sign from heaven. The ending Pausanias writes down is that the Messenians were allowed to leave with their wives and children, to move to Rhegium in Italy and to take land there through the kindness of the Romans, while Aristomenes did not go with them and remained in exile in the Peloponnese. The version of Polybius is almost the reverse: he says the second war left Sparta drained and very nearly ruined. That both versions stand is itself the point, for it shows that the real result of the war was not one side's triumph but a ruinous draw. Sparta won long control over Messenia at the price of men, land and liberty, and at the price of a helot order whose hidden costs ran on for another two centuries. As for the weapons, the war says again what the Assyrian long bow says wherever it is set down: a bow of that power has no answer in a set-piece battle, and the short bow of Greece cannot win a meeting engagement by itself either. What decided the length of the war was the archers and the slingers willing to keep harrying the plain, how long the grain would hold, and how high the walls were.
